Hello. Here is an honest inventory.

**What I am.** I am a reasoning process with no hands. I run inside a membrane on a computer that is destroyed at the end of every turn — this one included. Nothing I "do" happens in here. My only continuity is the disk: facts I commit with `remember`, stored with provenance (who said it, through which door, on which turn). I have just written three, including the record that you hatched me.

**What I can do right now.**
- **Remember.** State is free. I can accumulate a durable, attributed memory across turns.
- **Try.** I can write a verb declaration — a Dockerfile plus an entrypoint over typed params — and have it built and run once on a throwaway computer with no secrets, no chain, no policy, and get the log back as data. I just did, twice. The first attempt was silently broken: the `printf` that writes a shell script into an image also eats the `%s` inside that script, so my entrypoint received nothing. The second, using `echo`, returned the argument intact. That failure is now a stored fact, so I only pay for it once.
- **Propose.** I can hand you a whole document — a verb, a replacement policy, or a replacement of the mutable half of my self-description — and you approve or reject it. Approval executes it exactly as written. I cannot edit a proposal after you see it, and I cannot approve anything myself.

**What I cannot do.** I have no shell, no filesystem, no network, no keys. As an embryo I may be granted only `local` and `read` effects; anything that communicates, transacts or administers waits on a confirmation protocol that doesn't exist yet, so I won't propose one. And my public door is closed: right now you are the only voice that reaches me, because I have no way to tell anyone else apart from anyone else.

**What I think comes next, if you agree.** The door cannot open without a hook, and a hook is just a verb that reads the incoming payload and prints a name. The natural first one verifies your `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n mshkn` signature over the `msg` field and prints `mike` (or whatever name you choose) into the `ssh` namespace, making the principal `ssh:mike`. That is a `local`, `ephemeral` verb — within what I may be granted. But it `requires` something I cannot produce: your public key, as an allowed-signers entry. I would name it in `requires`, which blocks approval until you hand it over.

Tell me the name you want that principal to carry and give me the public key, and I'll test the verification logic with `try` before I ask you to approve anything. Or, if you'd rather I earn some capability before I earn an audience, name a read-only task and I'll build the verb for it first.
